messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: latency-slo-triggered | p95 tokens/response exceeded 1.2s in us-west-2 across routing group `prod-global-routing`. Triggered at 2391112223. Paging on-call @ops_oncall. Link: https://console.redwood/alerts/2391112223

ops_oncall: on it, paging SREs. @Carla can you join? I'm grabbing the dashboard.

Carla: joining. seeing a bunch of rapid reroute events in the last 6m. p95 spikes correlate with model-switch operations.

Zhang: Oof. logs showing repeated policy-eval -> reroute -> fallback -> reroute loops. suspect routing hysteresis config is effectively 0s.

emily: @ops_oncall @Carla is there customer impact? Any 5xxs or just slow responses?

ops_oncall: primary symptom: elevated p95 and increased tail latencies. Some request timeouts for long-context sessions. No large spike in 5xxs yet. Support flagged degraded UX for AcmeCorp chat flows.

pagerduty: Paging: escalation to SRE primary (Carla) acknowledged.

sre-bot: Incident created INC-2026-239111 | severity: high | channel: #incidents | runbook: routing-oscillation

Carla: quick snapshot from redispatch logs:

```
[2391112210] policy_eval: route=us-west-2 variant=redwood-7b-quant score=0.78
[2391112212] reroute -> us-east-1 variant=redwood-7b-quant
[2391112213] policy_eval: route=us-west-2 variant=redwood-7b-quant score=0.79
[2391112214] reroute -> us-east-1 variant=redwood-7b-quant
[2391112215] fallback -> redwood-7b-quant-compat (higher mem)
```

Carla: you can see the loop, decisions flip every 1-2s.

Zhang: config check: routing policy for prod-global-routing has hysteresis_ms: 0 and trigger_count_window: 1. Looks like previous change removed hysteresis accidentally.

emily: that explains it — tiny metric jitter will flip the route immediately.

ops_oncall: immediate mitigation options?

Carla: 1) Temporarily disable automatic reroute (set `enabled=false`) for prod-global-routing 2) Increase hysteresis_ms to 30000 and trigger_count_window to 3 3) Pin critical customers (AcmeCorp) to a stable variant/region until full rollback.

Zhang: I'm preparing CLI patch. putting it in a canary change to avoid config drift.

Carla: I'll open the handoff with SM and Support.

Zhang: CLI patch:

```
redwoodctl routing update --name prod-global-routing \
  --set hysteresis_ms=30000 --set trigger_count_window=3 --set enabled=true
```

Zhang: executing now (canary -> all): `redwoodctl routing apply --canary prod-global-routing`

ops_oncall: @Zhang confirm canary applied?

Zhang: canary applied to 2 routes. monitoring.

Carla: while that runs, I'm going to pin AcmeCorp sessions to `us-west-2:redwood-7b-quant` via override until stability.

support-ps: noted. I'll notify AcmeCorp support contact and let them know we're investigating and applying temporary pin. ETA for rollback window ~5m.

Carla: override command:

```
redwoodctl customer override set --customer acmecorp --route us-west-2 --variant redwood-7b-quant
```

Carla: override in place.

sre-bot: config-change detected: prod-global-routing hysteresis_ms=30000 trigger_count_window=3 (change id cfg-77661)

Zhang: after canary, p95 dropped from 1.45s -> 0.62s across canary routes. No new reroute cycles observed in canary.

ops_oncall: roll to remaining routes in 60s if stable.

Carla: rolling to full fleet now.

Zhang: rollout complete. monitoring graph: p95 trending down. no policy flaps since 2391112488.

emily: any note about wrong model variant? earlier chatter about variant compatibility fallback increasing latency.

Carla: root cause: two interacting misconfigs: 1) hysteresis removed in a recent deploy (policy change) 2) a fallback mapping from `redwood-7b-quant` -> `redwood-7b-quant-compat` triggered under memory pressure; the compat variant has higher CPU and increased token latency.

Carla: combination created a thrash: minor metric jitter triggered reroute, heavy fallback to compat variant, which then raised latency, which triggered reroute back — loop.

ops_oncall: customer impact assessment:
- AcmeCorp: chat sessions experienced 10-20% request timeouts and ~2x tail latency for ~12 minutes before override.
- Platform-wide: 2% of requests saw p95 > SLO in that window, no data loss, no 5xx spike.

support-ps: AcmeCorp support notified (INC:245-A), they're escalating internally but appreciate quick mitigation. We'll follow up with RCA and timeline.

Carla: next steps:
- Postmortem with timeline + config diff (assigned to Carla)
- Revert the change that removed hysteresis in the deploy pipeline and add test coverage (Zhang)
- Add automated guardrail preventing hysteresis_ms=0 for production routing policies (emily)
- Ensure fallback variants list includes explicit latency profiles to avoid swapping to expensive fallbacks without capacity checks (SRE)

ops_oncall: any follow-up mitigations in infra? autoscaling tweak?

Zhang: we'll also adjust autoscaler to react to steady windowed CPU rather than instantaneous spikes to avoid fallback thrash.

Carla: asking exec: recommend contacting impacted customers with a short summary and ETA for full postmortem.

emily: I'll add the postmortem template to the incident doc and schedule a meeting with affected owners.

pagerduty: Incident INC-2026-239111 acknowledged resolved by on-call at 2391112540. (status: mitigated)

Carla: marking incident mitigated. leaving the overrides in place for 1 hour and then we'll remove with controlled validation.

support-ps: AcmeCorp confirms improvement, thanks team :thumbsup: 

Zhang: removing canary overrides after 1h, will include change id in postmortem.

Carla: thanks everyone. I'll draft the incident report and include artifact links: dashboard, logs, cfg-77661, and timeline. Assigning follow-ups in the doc.

ops_oncall: handoff to follow-up rotation. please comment in INC-2026-239111 with any open action items.
